keep_with_next=True: Word keeps this paragraph on the same page as the one after it.

Footnotes and Endnotes

Comments

Comments are annotations attached to specific points in the document text. In HTML they render as superscript reference markers (orange brackets) and a comment section at the bottom of the page. In DOCX they appear in the Word review pane.

This sentence has a comment from Alice[1]Alice · 2026-04-17T09:00:00ZThis is a great example! attached at the end.

This sentence has a comment from Bob[2]Bob · 2026-04-17T10:00:00ZConsider adding more detail here. for review.

Track Changes

Track changes records insertions and deletions made by reviewers. In HTML, insertions render as green underlined text and deletions as red strikethrough text. In DOCX they appear in Word's review pane.

The original revenue figure was $3.8 M$4.2 M for the quarter.

Please reviewapprove this change before the deadline.

Page Breaks

An explicit page break element follows. In HTML it renders as <div class="dw-page-break"> (invisible, preserved for round-trip). In Word / LibreOffice it forces a new page.

This paragraph is immediately after the explicit page break. In Word it should appear at the top of a new page.

Page Number Fields

Page number fields can appear anywhere in the body, not just headers/footers. The paragraph below uses PAGE and NUMPAGES fields:

You are on page 1 of 1 total pages.

In HTML these render as <span class="dw-field" data-dw-field="PAGE">1</span> placeholders (static). In Word they update to the actual page number.

Headers and Footers

This document has a default header and footer defined at the Document level. The header (top of each page in Word) shows the document title in italics. The footer (bottom of each page) shows 'Page N of M'.

In HTML, headers and footers are rendered as <header> and <footer> elements. Page-number-only footer paragraphs are hidden (display:none) in the browser but survive the HTML → DOCX round-trip so Word can display the correct values.
